headline: Abandoned-cart recovery and a footer heading-order accessibility fix
summary: Two changes. Abandoned-cart recovery: a scheduled pass now finds carts left idle with items and no order and emails the shopper a link back — composed from the cart-abandonment scanner and a multi-step recovery sequence, gated on marketing consent (anyone who has withdrawn marketing consent is skipped) and idempotent (one email per abandonment, no double-sends across ticks). It stays completely inert until an SMTP mailer and an email resolver are configured, so a store without them is unaffected; the existing once-a-minute cron drives it. Separately, an accessibility fix: the footer column headings were emitted as h4 directly under the page's h2, skipping h3 — they are now h2 (the footer is a top-level landmark), so every storefront page has a clean, gap-free heading order. The footer looks identical.

items.title: Abandoned-cart recovery
items.body: A scheduled pass detects carts that have items, no paid order, and have been idle past a configurable threshold (`shop.cart_recovery_after_hours`, default 4h), then emails a recovery link to shoppers whose address is known. Enrolment is gated on the marketing-consent ledger and the send path honors the suppression list, so a withdrawn or unsubscribed shopper is never contacted; sends are idempotent. The pass no-ops cleanly until an SMTP mailer (`SMTP_HOST` / `MAIL_FROM`) and an email resolver are wired, so deploying it changes nothing until you opt in.

items.title: Footer heading order
items.body: The footer column headings ("Shop", "Framework", "Your account") were rendered as `h4` immediately after the page's `h2`, skipping `h4`'s prerequisite levels — a WCAG 1.3.1 heading-hierarchy violation. They are now `h2` (correct for a top-level region inside the footer landmark), giving a clean `h1 → h2 → h3` order on every page. The footer's appearance is unchanged.
